messages:
sasha: heads up — since the kernel+driver rollout last night (around 03:15 UTC) we're seeing a cluster of job failures and degraded multi‑GPU throughput on a subset of A100 hosts. cudaMalloc intermittently fails and NCCL jobs drop to single‑GPU speeds. tagging infra.

pranay: which hosts exactly? any node IDs, zone?

sasha: quick list from monitoring: a100-nyc-03, a100-nyc-07, a100-chi-02. all Ampere 80GB. failures started ~03:20 and spike aligns with rollout window.

jamie: ran topo check on a affected node, looks like peer links are not being advertised between GPUs. paste: 
```
# nvidia-smi topo --matrix
        GPU0 GPU1 GPU2 GPU3
GPU0     X   NV1  PHB  PHB
GPU1   NV1    X   PHB  PHB
GPU2   PHB  PHB   X   PHB
GPU3   PHB  PHB  PHB   X
```
this is wrong for these boards (expected NV2 or SYS links for NVLINK-enabled pairs).

lee: also saw an lspci detail that changed after the update — BAR1 reported accessible window is ~128MB instead of 256MB. snippet: 
```
02:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA Corporation Device
  Region 1: Memory at df000000 (64-bit, non-prefetchable) [size=128M]
  BAR1: size=0x08000000
```
which matches the MMIO window shrinkage hypothesis.

infra-bot: kernel-rollout job kernel-5.19.12 -> nodeset ampere-a100 completed at 02:58 UTC. drivers staged: nvidia-driver-535.* pushed.

deploy-bot: driver rollout log: 
```
[02:55] start driver push (canary)
[02:58] canary success (3 nodes)
[03:10] bulk push started
[03:18] 20% nodes completed
[03:22] automation: mark complete
```

pranay: so timeline aligns. suspect combination of kernel mmio remap + driver expecting larger BAR1 triggers P2P mapping failing. Could also be PCIe ACS/ACS override changed behavior — devices getting isolated at fabric layer.

jamie: confirmed on one host: /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:02:00.0/remove_peer_access shows peers lost. quick check: 
```
for d in /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:02:00.*/; do cat $d/peer_access 2>/dev/null || true; done
# output: mostly empty on affected hosts
```

lee: workaround idea — revert driver to previous build on a small canary set or revert kernel on those hosts. rolling full rollback will cost capacity but keeps jobs healthy.

tina: cost note — if we scale to single‑GPU jobs to avoid multi‑GPU, cost estimate +40% due to pod spike and longer runtimes. ops budget already tight this month.

pranay: do a targeted rollback on the 3 worst nodes first (NYC-03, NYC-07, CHI-02). I'll open rollback play and coordinate. please collect dmesg + nvidia-smi topo + lspci -vvv from each host before change.

sasha: grabbing logs now, will paste to the incident ticket. attaching quick dmesg snippets showing MMIO mapping warnings.

jamie: filing a kernel-driver compatibility issue in infra/bugtracker linking to these snippets. cc @eng-runtime and @eng-ml for model jobs impact.

infra-bot: incident incident-2028-03-a100-mmio created by pranay. link: internal/INC-3579 (private).

deploy-bot: starting targeted rollback to driver-525.60 on a100-nyc-03 at 03:50 UTC (canary). will monitor NCCL throughput.

lee: reminder: don't flip ACS settings cluster-wide without approval — that can hide PCIe isolation but break multitenancy/security. we should prefer driver/kernel rollback first.

pranay: agreed. if rollback fixes it we'll schedule a proper bisection next week to find the exact commit causing BAR1 shrinkage.

tina: noted budget impact and alerted finance — they want a postmortem with estimated extra GPU-hours.

sasha: thanks all — stanby while canary runs. i'll update thread with results. :hourglass:
